title: Separate hosting account from recipient account in should_deliver
description:
Spec sync to jmap-chat-spec 63e9d08 (diff 0cd3af0..63e9d08). Oracle: the quoted spec text at 63e9d08.

[vtc] Separate hosting account from recipient account in should_deliver
Spec (3cbb0c4): draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-wss-00.md L297-299: the event accountId is "the id of the call's hosting account ... This is usually not the recipient's personal account." Blocking (L340-352) is checked against "the recipient's contact list".
Code: crate-jmap-vtc-server/src/ephemeral.rs:183-268; crate-jmap-chat-vtc-server/src/lib.rs:266-292; crate-jmap-chat-vtc-server/src/lib.rs:321-337
Now: should_deliver uses one account_id for fetch_call and the participant lookup (the hosting account) and for is_user_blocked. is_blocked_by_contact reads the ChatContacts of that account, so with hosting accounts it consults the call owner's block list, not the recipient's.
Change: Give should_deliver (and should_deliver_vtc) the hosting account (from event.accountId) and the recipient's account separately. Use the recipient's account for is_user_blocked.
Verifier correction: Either give should_deliver/should_deliver_vtc separate hosting and recipient account ids, or document that VtcBackend::is_user_blocked must resolve the recipient's own contact list from `caller` and not from `account_id`, and change chat-vtc is_blocked_by_contact to match.
